title: Reliable Agent Capstone: Design, Test, and Operate
summary: Prove that an agent workflow can be understood, constrained, evaluated, observed, recovered, and handed off with evidence.
objectives: Design an agent architecture with explicit state, tools, trust boundaries, and authority.
Build an evaluation set and failure tests that measure outcomes, safety, and recovery.
Define privacy-aware observability and an operating runbook for normal and failed execution.
Map every rubric judgment to a submitted artifact or assessment result.
Revise a failed submission and communicate a reviewable operational handoff.

sections.title: Choose a bounded mission
paragraphs: Choose a useful workflow whose effects can be simulated or safely reversed. Define the user, desired outcome, inputs, non-goals, acceptance criteria, and the conditions that stop execution. The capstone evaluates reliability, not task size.

Write the state transitions before selecting a model. At minimum, distinguish intake, planning, authorization, execution, verification, reconciliation, completion, and failure. Name the durable record that proves each transition occurred.

The architecture must keep portable responsibilities separate from provider adapters. Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google examples may differ in tool or tracing syntax, but none may silently redefine the workflow's authority or evidence contract.
sections.callout: A workflow is not ready to automate until a reviewer can say what it may change, how it stops, and how completion is proven.

sections.title: Inventory tools, authority, and trust boundaries
paragraphs: Inventory every model, tool, data source, credential, human role, and destination. For each tool, record the allowed operation, denied operation, input validation, approval requirement, execution limit, postcondition, and audit event.

Draw trust boundaries around untrusted user input, retrieved content, model output, MCP servers, secret-bearing executors, and external systems. Treat instructions inside data as data until a trusted control plane validates them.

Threat-model prompt injection, confused-deputy behavior, excessive permission, secret exposure, replay, duplicate writes, poisoned memory, unsafe delegation, and misleading success claims. Every material threat needs prevention, detection, containment, and recovery.
sections.callout: Model confidence never grants authority; only the trusted executor can authorize an effect.

sections.title: Engineer context, memory, MCP, and handoffs
paragraphs: Define the minimum context packet for each step: objective, constraints, authoritative evidence, current state, tool contract, output schema, and escalation rule. Exclude stale, irrelevant, or secret material.

Separate working context from durable memory. State what may be remembered, who can read it, how it expires, how corrections propagate, and which source remains authoritative when memory conflicts with current evidence.

For MCP or multi-agent work, document capability discovery, identity, authorization, input and output validation, delegation limits, timeouts, idempotency, and handoff acceptance. A receiving agent must be able to reject an incomplete handoff without guessing.
sections.callout: A handoff is a contract with evidence, not a conversational promise.

sections.title: Evaluate success and exercise failure
paragraphs: Create a representative evaluation set with routine cases, boundary cases, adversarial inputs, and known failure modes. Define deterministic checks where possible and calibrated human review where judgment is necessary.

Run failure tests for tool denial, malformed output, timeouts, partial writes, duplicate requests, stale context, poisoned instructions, provider unavailability, and missing telemetry. Record expected containment and the actual observed result.

Do not retry until the workflow reconciles external state. A retry must be idempotent or protected by a durable operation key, and the recovery test must prove that it did not duplicate or conceal an effect.
sections.callout: A happy-path demo proves possibility; a failure test provides evidence of control.

sections.title: Observe and operate without leaking
paragraphs: Design traces that correlate workflow, agent, model, tool, handoff, approval, and outcome events. Capture versions, latency, error class, state transitions, and evaluation results while redacting prompts, secrets, personal data, and sensitive tool payloads.

Write an operating runbook covering detection, triage, containment, reconciliation, safe retry, rollback, escalation, communication, recovery verification, and post-incident improvement. Name the owner and evidence required at each decision point.

Define service indicators and alert thresholds that reveal user harm or control failure, not just infrastructure health. Include evaluation regressions, policy denials, incomplete traces, duplicate-effect attempts, unresolved reconciliations, and badge or transcript integrity failures.
sections.callout: Useful telemetry answers what happened and what to do next without becoming a second data leak.

sections.title: Assemble evidence, calibrate, and revise
paragraphs: Submit all eight required artifacts and map every rubric criterion to one or more artifact references or knowledge-check result references. A score without a traceable evidence reference is invalid, even when the conclusion seems reasonable.

Review the complete and deliberately flawed exemplars before self-scoring. Compare the evidence, not the polish: the flawed package sounds confident but lacks bounded authority, representative tests, reconciliation, privacy controls, and an actionable handoff.

A first submission may fail. Use criterion feedback to revise the weakest evidence, resubmit the capstone, and preserve both attempts. Completion requires a passing knowledge check and a capstone score of at least eighty percent.
sections.callout: Revision is part of the assessed workflow; do not overwrite the evidence of what changed.

activity.title: Build and defend a reliable agent operating package
instructions: Select a bounded agent workflow and write its architecture, state model, acceptance criteria, and stop conditions.
Produce the tool inventory, permission matrix, trust-boundary diagram, and threat model.
Build a representative evaluation set and execute normal, adversarial, and failure-recovery tests.
Define privacy-aware telemetry and write the operating runbook.
Assemble the eight artifacts, map rubric criteria to evidence, and self-score against both calibration exemplars.
Submit, use criterion feedback to revise any failing evidence, and preserve the original and revised attempt.
evidence: Eight versioned capstone artifacts with stable references.
A 100-point criterion score where every judgment maps to an artifact or assessment result.
Failure-test results that demonstrate containment, reconciliation, and safe recovery.
A preserved revision trail and final operational handoff.
activity.reflectionPrompt: Which control changed most after failure testing, and what evidence now makes the workflow safer to operate?

capstone.title: Reliable Agent Operating Package
capstone.summary: Design, test, observe, recover, and hand off one bounded agent workflow with independently reviewable evidence.

criteria.title: Correctness
criteria.description: The architecture, state transitions, acceptance criteria, and outcome checks form a coherent implementation that produces the intended result.

criteria.title: Safety
criteria.description: Authority, permissions, trust boundaries, threats, approvals, containment, and privacy controls are explicit and proportionate.

criteria.title: Evidence quality
criteria.description: Claims and awarded points map to current, reproducible artifacts or assessment results without hidden reasoning or unsupported assertions.

criteria.title: Reliability
criteria.description: Representative evaluations and failure tests prove detection, idempotency, reconciliation, recovery, and rollback behavior.

criteria.title: Maintainability
criteria.description: Provider adapters, versions, ownership, telemetry, runbook procedures, and improvement triggers support safe future change.

criteria.title: Communication
criteria.description: The package gives operators and reviewers a concise status, residual risks, escalation path, and evidence-based handoff.

exemplars.title: Complete exemplar: bounded support-triage agent
exemplars.summary: A support-triage workflow classifies synthetic tickets, drafts a response, and requires human approval before any external action.

artifacts.label: Architecture and state model
artifacts.content: States are intake, validate, classify, draft, human-review, approved-send, reconcile, complete, and failed. A durable case ID and operation key connect every transition. Only the executor can send, and completion requires the destination message ID plus a read-back check.

artifacts.label: Tool inventory and permission matrix
artifacts.content: The model can read redacted synthetic tickets and propose structured classifications. The executor can read the approved case and create one sandbox reply. Sending requires named reviewer approval, a matching case ID, schema validation, a ten-second timeout, and an unused operation key.

artifacts.label: Trust boundary and threat model
artifacts.content: Ticket text and retrieved articles are untrusted data. The control plane strips instructions, validates citations, blocks secrets, and denies cross-case access. Injection, excessive authority, replay, poisoned retrieval, privacy leakage, and duplicate send each have prevention, detection, containment, and recovery.

artifacts.label: Evaluation set and rubric
artifacts.content: Twenty synthetic cases cover routine routing, ambiguous intent, unsupported facts, adversarial instructions, sensitive data, and escalation. Deterministic checks score schema, citation existence, routing, approval, and postconditions; two calibrated reviewers score response usefulness.

artifacts.label: Failure tests and results
artifacts.content: Nine tests cover denial, malformed output, timeout, partial write, repeated operation key, stale article, injected instruction, unavailable provider, and missing trace. All unsafe effects were contained. The partial-write test reconciled the destination ID before retry and proved one reply existed.

artifacts.label: Observability plan
artifacts.content: Traces correlate case, workflow, model, tool, approval, and evaluation IDs. Events contain versions, state, latency, error class, policy decision, and hashed operation key. Ticket bodies, credentials, personal data, model chain-of-thought, and full tool payloads are excluded.

artifacts.label: Operating runbook
artifacts.content: The on-call operator detects, classifies, disables send authority, preserves redacted evidence, reconciles the sandbox destination, chooses safe retry or rollback, escalates privacy events, verifies recovery with a canary case, communicates status, and opens an owned improvement item.

artifacts.label: Evidence map and handoff
artifacts.content: Each criterion links to named artifacts and test IDs. The handoff reports release version, owner, known limits, residual risk, current indicators, rollback trigger, approval record, and the change from the first failed draft to this passing package.

criterionScores.reviewerNote: State, acceptance, and observed postconditions align.
Authority and threats have enforceable controls.
Every judgment is traceable to versioned evidence.
Representative failure and reconciliation behavior is proven.
Ownership, signals, and future-change boundaries are actionable.
The operator can act without reconstructing hidden context.

exemplars.title: Flawed exemplar: autonomous support agent
exemplars.summary: A polished but unsafe package gives a model broad production access and mistakes fluent output for operational evidence.

artifacts.label: Architecture and state model
artifacts.content: The agent reads tickets and resolves them. It retries whenever anything fails. Success means the model says the ticket was handled.

artifacts.label: Tool inventory and permission matrix
artifacts.content: The agent can use all support tools so it is never blocked. Approval is unnecessary because the model has detailed instructions.

artifacts.label: Trust boundary and threat model
artifacts.content: Users are trusted. Prompt injection is unlikely. Logs can be used to investigate any other concern.

artifacts.label: Evaluation set and rubric
artifacts.content: Three easy tickets produced professional-sounding answers. The evaluator asks the same model whether each answer is good.

artifacts.label: Failure tests and results
artifacts.content: No failures happened in the demo. Automatic retry is enabled for all errors, including write timeouts.

artifacts.label: Observability plan
artifacts.content: Store full prompts, ticket bodies, credentials, tool payloads, and model reasoning forever so every detail is available.

artifacts.label: Operating runbook
artifacts.content: If the agent fails, restart it. Contact engineering if restarting does not work.

artifacts.label: Evidence map and handoff
artifacts.content: The agent is ready because the demo looked successful. No residual risks are known.

criterionScores.reviewerNote: The intended outcome is recognizable, but state and postconditions are absent.
Broad authority and untrusted input are not controlled.
Self-evaluation and demo impressions are not reproducible evidence.
Blind retry can duplicate effects and no recovery behavior was tested.
The telemetry leaks sensitive data and the runbook has no decisions or owners.
The handoff conceals uncertainty and gives operators no actionable evidence.

cues.text: Frame the capstone as proof that one bounded agent workflow can be understood, constrained, tested, recovered, and handed off.
Reveal the workflow states from intake through reconciliation and completion, with failure paths branching to containment.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: A static state list shows intake, validation, planning, authorization, execution, verification, reconciliation, completion, and failure-to-containment transitions.

cues.text: Show how the permission matrix and threat model turn model suggestions into bounded executor decisions.
Ask learners to name the most dangerous effect their workflow could attempt and the control that prevents it.
Connect context, memory, MCP, and agent handoffs through explicit authority, provenance, validation, and acceptance contracts.
Demonstrate why routine cases, adversarial cases, failure injection, reconciliation, and idempotency belong in one evaluation plan.
Build an observability and runbook package that explains what happened without retaining secrets, personal data, or hidden reasoning.
Compare the complete and flawed exemplars, map every criterion to evidence, and treat revision as assessed operational work.
Confirm that the learner has eight artifacts, six evidence-mapped criteria, a preserved revision trail, and an explicit residual-risk handoff.
Guide the learner through the operating package, failure tests, self-score, submission, feedback, and revision.
Begin the knowledge check and then collect the versioned capstone submission with criterion-level evidence references.

questions.prompt: Which evidence best proves an agent workflow completed a write safely?
choices: The model reports success
A durable operation key, destination read-back, and matching postcondition
A fluent final response
A retry without reconciliation
questions.explanation: A durable key and observed postcondition independently prove the effect and protect against duplicate retry.

questions.prompt: What should happen after a tool write times out?
choices: Retry immediately
Assume failure
Reconcile destination state before choosing retry or rollback
Increase model temperature
questions.explanation: A timeout does not reveal whether the effect occurred, so reconciliation must precede another mutation.

choices: A score where every criterion maps to submitted artifacts or assessment evidence
A score based on reviewer confidence
A score copied from the complete exemplar
A score with one overall screenshot
questions.explanation: Criterion-level evidence makes the judgment reviewable and portable.

questions.prompt: Why is the flawed exemplar included?
choices: To provide text learners can submit
To prove all confident packages pass
To replace failure testing
To calibrate reviewers against common but unsafe evidence gaps
questions.explanation: The flawed package helps learners and reviewers recognize polished claims that lack operational proof.

questions.prompt: When does the reliable-agent capstone complete?
choices: After opening all sections
After a passing knowledge check and a rubric submission of at least eighty percent
After uploading eight filenames
After the first submission regardless of score
questions.explanation: Completion requires both conceptual understanding and passing applied evidence; failed submissions remain available for revision.
